claims.text: FROM uses the base image's layers; RUN, COPY and ADD each create a layer holding that step's file changes; instructions such as EXPOSE, ENV and LABEL only record metadata (0B rows in docker history).
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: image layers / Dockerfile reference / docker history

claims.text: The build cache reuses a step's layer when the instruction and its parent layer are unchanged (and, for COPY/ADD, the copied files are unchanged); once a step misses the cache, every later step is rebuilt.
scripts/up.sh runs docker compose up with --build every time, and later runs reuse the lab image's cached layers.
docker history donhang-lab:stage-0 shows the RUN /bin/sh -c apk add --no-cache ... step on top (about 12.7MB), with the base image's rows below, some of size 0B.
claims.source_hint: generator check on the running lab (12.7MB)

claims.text: Changing the apk add list reruns only that step (base reused); changing the FROM version rebuilds every layer above it.
Steps that rarely change belong near the top of a Dockerfile so small changes rebuild little.
